instruction: Place an order for all wrench sets in my amazon wish list.
notes: Single-app task (amazon). Flow: get passwords, log in, read the wish list, clear any pre-existing cart contents (so the order contains only wrench sets; CartEntry/WishListEntry changes are not evaluated), move every wish-list entry of product_type 'wrench set' to the cart with its wish-list quantity, look up a payment card and an address, place one order, then complete the task with no answer. The problem instantiates two wrench-set entries plus one non-wrench entry as placeholders; at runtime the agent must repeat the move action for every matching wish-list entry. The non-wrench product must stay in the wish list (move requires is-wrench-set, and the goal keeps it wish-listed). clear_cart requires (not (cart-clean)) and moves require (cart-clean), so clearing happens exactly once, before any move; moves and clear require (not (order-placed)), so all items are in the cart before place_order. (in-cart p q) records what was in the cart when the order was placed, i.e. the ordered product/quantity pairs. Because grounded product objects cannot be referenced from the domain, supervisor-complete-task's precondition carries the nullary goal condition (order-placed); the per-product goal facts live in the problem goal and, together with the ordering constraints above, still force complete_task to be the last action. show_payment_cards/show_addresses take the discovered record as an extra non-API parameter to assert known-payment-card/known-address.
